## Why

The encyclical *Fidentem Piumque Animum* champions the Rosary as the essential devotional tool for the faithful, emphasizing its power for persistent, communal prayer and its role in nurturing faith and seeking Christian unity. To capture this central meaning while maintaining perfect legibility and avoiding all abstraction, I have chosen to sculpt the primary object of the encyclical itself: a single, complete **Rosary**. This familiar devotional item embodies the entire message of persevering prayer and the meditation on Christ's life that Pope Leo XIII describes. A single, clearly defined Rosary is universally recognized, respects the "single-subject discipline," and avoids the "abstract, symbolic only through vague geometry, or dependent on explanation" forms forbidden in the prompt. I have specifically configured the Rosary with the Crucifix at the top, emphasizing the spiritual focus and providing a distinct sculptural apex, while its circular, looped form is rendered as a monumental, cohesive object for optimal legibility.

## Text-to-image prompt

A single, monumental, sculptural rosary, presented as a premium, photorealistic 3D render, perfectly centered on a transparent background with no environmental details. The rosary is composed of large, uniform beads made of polished, deep-blue lapis lazuli, interconnected by fine, articulated links of burnished 22k gold filigree. The beads are arranged in a large, unbroken loop that forms a cohesive circular object, viewed from a frontal perspective. At the very apex of the sculpture is a detailed, stylized Crucifix made of sculpted gold and dark ebony wood, featuring a clear figure of Christ. The circular form of the rosary, with its distinct decades of beads and five major connecting beads, is clearly defined. The entire sculpture rests upon a minimal, circular plinth made of polished white marble with faint grey veining. The texture of the lapis lazuli shows micro-fractures and mineral variations; the gold links are detailed with intricate filigree patterns. The lighting is high-contrast studio illumination, with a strong key light from the front-left creating deep shadows (chiaroscuro) and crisp highlights on the gold and bead surfaces. A pronounced ambient occlusion effect defines the contact points between beads, links, and the plinth. The camera angle is frontal, dead-center, using an 85mm lens with f/9 aperture, capturing the full object without distortion. No text, inscriptions, or lettering are visible.
